subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Give the structures of A, B and C in the following reaction: C₆H₅N₂Cl —CuCN→ A —H₂O/H⁺→ B —NH₃, Δ→ C

verification.note: Unit 18 (Organic Compounds Containing Nitrogen) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.115-120, from the shaded sub-box "ORGANIC COMPOUNDS CONTAINING NITROGEN" of printed chapter 12 ("12. ORGANIC CHEMISTRY"); the book prints this question on book p.115 as VSAQ 7. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK CHECK: the printed answer A = C₆H₅CN, B = C₆H₅COOH, C = C₆H₅CONH₂ is CORRECT and is kept. BOOK GAPS, filled here: (1) the printed answer writes the last arrow straight from benzoic acid to benzamide, skipping ammonium benzoate — the salt forms first and only loses water on heating, so the card writes both stages; (2) the first step is a Sandmeyer reaction and gives off N₂ and CuCl, neither of which the book writes; (3) the hydrolysis of a nitrile needs two water molecules and releases ammonia, which the book also omits. EQUATIONS CHECKED: C₆H₅CN + 2H₂O → C₆H₅COOH + NH₃ balances C 7/7, H 9/9, N 1/1, O 2/2; C₆H₅COONH₄ → C₆H₅CONH₂ + H₂O balances C 7/7, H 9/9, N 1/1, O 2/2.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: A and B
steps.why: The first step is a Sandmeyer reaction: the –N₂⁺ group leaves as nitrogen gas and the cyanide group takes its place on the ring. The second step is the ordinary acid hydrolysis of a nitrile, which turns –CN into –COOH and releases ammonia.
common_mistakes: Writing A as an isocyanide, C₆H₅–NC. Cuprous cyanide gives the nitrile, joined through carbon.
Forgetting that nitrogen gas leaves in the first step. Every diazonium replacement gives off N₂.
steps.memory_tip: Diazonium plus CuCN gives the nitrile; water and acid then turn every nitrile into the acid.
steps.margin_note: Name A and B in words as well as in formulae. Benzonitrile and benzoic acid are the marked words.

steps.label: C, with the equations
lines: Ammonia first gives the ammonium salt:
On heating the salt loses water:
steps.why: Ammonia is a base and benzoic acid is an acid, so the first thing formed is the salt ammonium benzoate. Only when that salt is heated does it lose a water molecule to give the amide. Writing the amide straight from the acid skips the step the Δ in the question stands for.
common_mistakes: Writing C as ammonium benzoate. That is the intermediate; heating it gives the amide, which is C.
Leaving out the water in the second equation. The amide is one water molecule lighter than the salt.
steps.memory_tip: Acid plus ammonia gives the ammonium salt; heat removes water and leaves the amide.
steps.margin_note: The Δ over the last arrow is the mark. Show the ammonium salt and then the loss of water.

insider_note: The three answers are benzonitrile, benzoic acid and benzamide. The step most often shortened is benzoic acid to benzamide — ammonia gives ammonium benzoate first, and only heating turns that into benzamide, which is what the Δ in the question is asking for.
